text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.

- The electoral campaign for Macedonia's local elections is in its last week. There will be 14,146 candidates, or 1 percent of the Macedonian polulation contesting the election. Out of this number, 655 candidates are running for mayors in 121 municipalities and 13,491 candidates for councillors in municipal assemblies. They are proposed by 33 political parties, nine coalitions and groups of voters.
- Funds from the PHARE programme to be distributed to small and medium companies and to support the agricultural sector, the government said on Monday.

- Trade between Australia and Macedonia has increased in the past five years, said president of the Macedonian Chamber of Commerce Dusan Petreski on Monday at a meeting with Australian businessmen. Macedonia had a huge deficit with Australia in 1995, its imports stood at $11.7 million and exports only at $800,000.

- The Holy Synod of the Macedonian Orthodox Church expressed readiness for cooperation with the Holy Synod of the Serbian Orthodox church but rejected all denials of the existence of the Macedonian church and nation expressed by some Serbian church circles.
